correctness.rationale: The explicit Gaussian integrated-quantile criterion reduces the finite two-, three-, four-, five-sign laws to binomial upper-tail cut points. All noncentral inequalities and strict scale separation have exact rational certificates from Machin pi and Taylor bounds, and central cuts are elementary algebra; the finite base checks are replayable from verification/checker.py. Convex order is preserved by scaling and independent convolution, and partitions n=2a+3b or n=3a+4b+5c prove all n in the two respective ranges. Sharpness is witnessed at n=2 by the upper-quantile cut p=1/4, and at n=3 by the p=1/2 cut (absolute-value loss). No numerical simulation is used to establish infinite claims.

originality.rationale: The precise sharp uniform factors for normalized iid Rademacher walks over all n>=2 and all n>=3 are not consequences of the sharp unrestricted sub-Gaussian theorem: that theorem has a strictly larger coefficient and an n=1 extremizer. Exact analysis for four base laws together with independent-block tensorization yields both sharp infinite-family claims. Full mathematical text of three adjacent primary papers and targeted mathematical-record/web searches were compared; no direct dominating or equivalent statement was found, while indexing risk persists.

value.rationale: The recent universal MGF-sub-Gaussian convex-order constant is sharp because of a single symmetric sign, motivating the precise question whether independent repeated averaging strictly lowers the sharp universal Gaussian dilation across all sample sizes beyond a threshold. The finding supplies two strict sharp refinements that hold simultaneously for every convex loss over infinite sample-size classes; a nontrivial finite-binomial certificate coupled with exact decomposition into independent blocks yields genuinely global conclusions. Distinct optimal witnesses at n=2 and n=3 explain the structural improvement; this is not a cosmetic rewriting of the general theorem.
